_about: Outside facts for the night-sky page (2026-11-18, D16). A row is written to the page only when every claim it makes carries a source: url, the source's own words (quote) and the day it was read (read), as scripts/site/pseo/facts.json requires. Filled from the Scout's rows of 2026-11-18 (chief docs/briefs/2026-11-18-scout-sky-facts.json: 51 of 64 claims verified); the unverified claims are cut or reworded as the Scout's return gives. The Scout's caveat stands on every web-page quote: read through a fetch that passes the page through a model, so close but not a byte copy; the five PDFs were read from their own text. A row's "held" names a claim the line no longer makes until a source is read.

wildlife.name: Great horned owl
wildlife.when: Around sunset ({ss}) and in the hours before sunrise ({sr}).
wildlife.what: Low, far-carrying hoots: hoo, hoo-hoo, hoo, hoo. Courtship calling begins in October and peaks in November and December.

sources.claim: Courtship calling October to February, peaking in November and December.
sources.name: NC Wildlife
sources.quote: Most calling occurs when courtship begins in October, with peak calling in November and December,
sources.note: NC Wildlife Resources Commission (primary, NC). Supports October start and the Nov to Dec peak. No source read today names February as the end; the page also says calls slow once eggs are laid. Read through WebFetch with a verbatim prompt; the tool passes the page through a model, so this is a read of the live page, not a byte copy.

wildlife.name: White-tailed deer
wildlife.when: The hour around sunset ({ss}) first, then around sunrise ({sr}).

inside.text: Georgia DNR's rut map, drawn from deer and vehicle collisions, puts peak deer movement in Lumpkin County at November 24 to 30: right now.

wildlife.what: In one South Carolina study, overall activity, and activity around sunrise and sunset, did not change with nearness to the new or full moon.

sources.claim: The hour around sunset first, then around sunrise.
sources.name: Sullivan and others, 2016
sources.quote: the crepuscular hours surrounding sunset appear to be when deer are most likely to be active
sources.note: Sullivan, Ditchkoff, Collier, Ruth, Raglin, "Movement with the Moon: White-tailed Deer Activity and Solunar Events", J. Southeastern Assoc. Fish and Wildlife Agencies 3:225-232 (2016), South Carolina. Abstract: "activity patterns are predominately crepuscular." Read by local text extraction of the PDF that WebFetch saved (byte-level, not a model); ligature glyphs restored (fi, ff, fl).

sources.claim: Overall deer activity, and activity around sunrise and sunset, did not change with nearness to the new or full moon.
sources.name: Sullivan and others, 2016
sources.quote: throughout the entire 24-hour period did not seem to be affected by proximity to the new or full moon
sources.note: Full sentence opens "Deer activity during day, night, around sunrise, around sunset, and". Male deer, GPS collars, Aug to Dec 2010 to 2012. Read by local text extraction of the PDF that WebFetch saved (byte-level, not a model); ligature glyphs restored (fi, ff, fl).

sources.claim: Lumpkin County's rut peaks about November 24 to 30.
sources.name: Georgia DNR rut map
sources.note: Georgia DNR rut map (primary). The map's table, under the heading "County Peak Dates" and the title "Peak Deer Movement in Georgia", reads Lumpkin then 11/24–11/30, with no asterisk (asterisk means fewer than 100 collisions). Read from the PDF's text layer; the digits use a custom font, decoded with the PDF's own ToUnicode map. PDF created 2014-09-18; dates come from deer-vehicle collisions, not a forecast for 2026. Neighbours: White, Habersham, Rabun 11/24–11/30; Dawson, Union 11/17–11/23; Hall 11/10–11/16. Supported wording: "Georgia DNR's rut map puts peak deer movement in Lumpkin County at November 24 to 30." The page shows this line from Nov 20 to Dec 3, wider than the source. Read by local text extraction of the PDF that WebFetch saved (byte-level, not a model); ligature glyphs restored (fi, ff, fl).
